LESSON_TWO_DIALOGUE_TWO.title: 對話二 · Dialogue 2
LESSON_TWO_DIALOGUE_TWO.setting: 星期五下課以後 · After class, Friday

text.traditional: 今天是星期五，明天是週末，你們要不要來我家？
text.simplified: 今天是星期五，明天是周末，你们要不要来我家？
text.pinyin: Jīntiān shì xīngqí wǔ, míngtiān shì zhōumò, nǐmen yào bú yào lái wǒ jiā?
text.english: Today is Friday and it is the weekend tomorrow. Do you want to come to my place?

text.traditional: 明天是九月二十三號……啊！是妳的生日！
text.simplified: 明天是九月二十三号……啊！是妳的生日！
text.pinyin: Míngtiān shì jiǔ yuè èrshísān hào... Ā! Shì nǐ de shēngrì!
text.english: It is September 23rd tomorrow... Ah! It is your birthday!

text.pinyin: Yíwén, shēngrì kuàilè!
text.english: Happy birthday, Yiwen!

text.traditional: 謝謝！明天晚上六點來我家，好不好？
text.simplified: 谢谢！明天晚上六点来我家，好不好？
text.pinyin: Xièxie! Míngtiān wǎnshang liù diǎn lái wǒ jiā, hǎo bù hǎo?
text.english: Thanks! How about coming to my place at 6 p.m. tomorrow?

text.pinyin: Méi wèntí.
text.english: No problem.

text.pinyin: Hǎo, míngtiān jiàn.
text.english: Okay, see you tomorrow.

comprehension.prompt: 宜文請大家幾點來她家？

LESSON_TWO_GRAMMAR_FIVE.lessonTitleEnglish: What Time Do You Go to School?
LESSON_TWO_GRAMMAR_FIVE.titleTraditional: 主語 + 想法 + 動作
LESSON_TWO_GRAMMAR_FIVE.titleEnglish: Put Wanting or Liking Before the Action
LESSON_TWO_GRAMMAR_FIVE.learnerPromise: Say what you want, like, or love to eat, drink, visit, or do.
LESSON_TWO_GRAMMAR_FIVE.explanation: Words like 要, 喜歡, and 愛 show what you want or feel about doing something. Put that word before the action word.

teachingGlossary.meaning: ending word for a yes/no question

discoveryLab.title: Put the feeling before the action
discoveryLab.description: Put the wanting or liking word first, then the action word.
discoveryLab.prompt: What meaning comes before the action?

choices.label: Want · 要 + 喝
choices.note: 要 tells your intention. 喝 names the action.

choices.label: Like · 喜歡 + 喝
choices.note: 喜歡 comes before the action 喝.

choices.label: Love · 愛 + 吃
choices.note: 愛 adds the feeling; 吃 still names the action.

choices.label: Repair the stack
choices.traditional: 我喝要茶。 → 我要喝茶。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ hē yào chá. → Wǒ yào hē chá.
choices.english: Repair it: I want to drink tea.
choices.note: Move 要 before the action 喝.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Intention or feeling first, action second.

patternRows.english: Do you want to go to the teacher’s home?

items.question: Why is 要 before 吃?
items.answer: 要 is the wanting word, and the wanting word goes before the action word: 要 + 吃, never 吃 + 要.

items.question: Can I use 愛 for any liking?
items.answer: No — 愛 means love, a very strong feeling. For a normal like, use 喜歡.

items.question: Where does 不 go with 愛喝?
items.answer: 不 goes before the wanting word, not the action: 不愛喝, never 愛不喝.

right.pinyin: Wǒ bú ài hē zhēnzhū nǎichá.
right.english: I do not love drinking bubble milk tea.

text.pinyin: Māma xǐhuān hē nǎichá.
text.english: Mom likes drinking milk tea.

text.pinyin: Nǐ yào qù lǎoshī jiā ma?
text.english: Do you want to go to the teacher’s home?

words.meaning: ending word for a yes/no question

examples.teachingNote: 不 stays with 愛; the following action still comes second.

text.traditional: 我愛吃水果，不愛喝珍珠奶茶。
text.simplified: 我爱吃水果，不爱喝珍珠奶茶。
text.pinyin: Wǒ ài chī shuǐguǒ, bú ài hē zhēnzhū nǎichá.
text.english: I love eating fruit and do not love drinking bubble milk tea.

I love drinking water.

questions.correctFeedback: 愛 gives the feeling before the action 喝.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 愛 + 喝, then name the drink.

LESSON_TWO_GRAMMAR_SIX.titleTraditional: 肯定 + 不／沒 + 肯定
LESSON_TWO_GRAMMAR_SIX.titleEnglish: Ask by Pairing Positive and Negative Forms
LESSON_TWO_GRAMMAR_SIX.learnerPromise: Ask natural choice questions such as “busy or not?” and “want to go or not?”
LESSON_TWO_GRAMMAR_SIX.explanation: Repeat the key doing or describing word around 不: 忙不忙, 吃不吃, 要不要. With 有, use 有沒有. This pattern already makes a question, so do not add 嗎.

teachingGlossary.meaning: do not have; there is not
the first syllable of 喜歡 in the source contraction
the second syllable of 喜歡
very; used before a describing word
ending word for a yes/no question

LESSON_TWO_GRAMMAR_SIX.pattern: Who + positive form + 不／沒 + positive form

discoveryLab.title: Let the verb ask both possibilities
discoveryLab.description: The repeated form presents a compact choice: yes or no.
discoveryLab.prompt: Which positive-negative family do you need?

choices.label: State · 忙不忙
choices.note: Repeat the describing word 忙 around 不.

choices.label: Action · 吃不吃
choices.english: Are you eating / Do you eat?
choices.note: Repeat the action word 吃 around 不.

choices.label: Have · 有沒有
choices.pinyin: Tā yǒu méi yǒu Táiwān péngyǒu?
choices.english: Does he have a Taiwanese friend?
choices.note: 有 uses its own negative 沒有, giving 有沒有.

choices.label: Do not add 嗎
choices.traditional: 你忙不忙嗎？ → 你忙不忙？
choices.simplified: 你忙不忙吗？ → 你忙不忙？
choices.pinyin: Nǐ máng bù máng ma? → Nǐ máng bù máng?
choices.note: The positive-negative pair already marks the sentence as a question.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Repeat the key form around its negative, and leave 嗎 out.

patternRows.english: Do you eat / Are you eating?

items.question: Why can’t I add 嗎 to 忙不忙?
items.answer: The pair 忙不忙 already makes the question. Adding 嗎 gives it two question marks.

items.question: Why is it 有沒有, not 有不有?
items.answer: 有 takes 沒有 as its negative, so the pair repeats 有 and 沒有. Never pair 有 with 不.

right.pinyin: Tā yǒu méi yǒu Táiwān péngyǒu?
right.english: Does he have a Taiwanese friend?

words.meaning: do not have; there is not

items.question: My friend said 我不要去他家. Why is 去不去 wrong?
items.answer: The pair repeats the key word in the reply — 要. Ask 要不要, not 去不去.

right.pinyin: Nǐ yào bú yào qù tā jiā?
right.english: Do you want to go to his home?

text.pinyin: Lǎoshī máng bù máng?
text.english: Is the teacher busy?

discoveryLab.description: The repeated form presents a compact choice: yes or no.
discoveryLab.prompt: Which positive-negative family do you need?

choices.label: State · 忙不忙
choices.note: Repeat the describing word 忙 around 不.

choices.label: Action · 吃不吃
choices.english: Are you eating / Do you eat?
choices.note: Repeat the action word 吃 around 不.

choices.label: Have · 有沒有
choices.pinyin: Tā yǒu méi yǒu Táiwān péngyǒu?
choices.english: Does he have a Taiwanese friend?
choices.note: 有 uses its own negative 沒有, giving 有沒有.

choices.label: Do not add 嗎
choices.traditional: 你忙不忙嗎？ → 你忙不忙？
choices.simplified: 你忙不忙吗？ → 你忙不忙？
choices.pinyin: Nǐ máng bù máng ma? → Nǐ máng bù máng?
choices.note: The positive-negative pair already marks the sentence as a question.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Repeat the key form around its negative, and leave 嗎 out.

patternRows.english: Do you eat / Are you eating?

items.question: Why can’t I add 嗎 to 忙不忙?
items.answer: The pair 忙不忙 already makes the question. Adding 嗎 gives it two question marks.

items.question: Why is it 有沒有, not 有不有?
items.answer: 有 takes 沒有 as its negative, so the pair repeats 有 and 沒有. Never pair 有 with 不.

right.pinyin: Tā yǒu méi yǒu Táiwān péngyǒu?
right.english: Does he have a Taiwanese friend?

items.question: My friend said 我不要去他家. Why is 去不去 wrong?
items.answer: The pair repeats the key word in the reply — 要. Ask 要不要, not 去不去.

dialogue.title: 對話二 · Dialogue 2
dialogue.setting: 星期五下課以後 · After class, Friday

text.traditional: 今天是星期五，明天是週末，你們要不要來我家？
text.simplified: 今天是星期五，明天是周末，你们要不要来我家？
text.pinyin: Jīntiān shì xīngqí wǔ, míngtiān shì zhōumò, nǐmen yào bú yào lái wǒ jiā?
text.english: Today is Friday and it is the weekend tomorrow. Do you want to come to my place?

text.traditional: 明天是九月二十三號……啊！是妳的生日！
text.simplified: 明天是九月二十三号……啊！是妳的生日！
text.pinyin: Míngtiān shì jiǔ yuè èrshísān hào... Ā! Shì nǐ de shēngrì!
text.english: It is September 23rd tomorrow... Ah! It is your birthday!

text.pinyin: Yíwén, shēngrì kuàilè!
text.english: Happy birthday, Yiwen!

text.traditional: 謝謝！明天晚上六點來我家，好不好？
text.simplified: 谢谢！明天晚上六点来我家，好不好？
text.pinyin: Xièxie! Míngtiān wǎnshang liù diǎn lái wǒ jiā, hǎo bù hǎo?
text.english: Thanks! How about coming to my place at 6 p.m. tomorrow?

text.pinyin: Méi wèntí.
text.english: No problem.

text.pinyin: Hǎo, míngtiān jiàn.
text.english: Okay, see you tomorrow.
